headline: Common Mistakes When Planning Kitchen Electrical
articleBody: When you're dreaming up your new kitchen, it's easy to get caught up in the fun stuff like countertops and cabinet colors. But overlooking the electrical planning can lead to some real headaches down the line. One big mistake is undercounting appliance loads. People often forget just how much power things like blenders, coffee makers, and toasters draw, especially when they're all used at once. Make sure you list out everything you'll plug in! Another common misstep is skipping dedicated circuits for high-wattage appliances. Your microwave, oven, or even that fancy new fridge might need its own circuit, and not planning for it means tripped breakers or worse. Placing too few outlets for countertop use is another classic. You'll thank yourself later for having plenty of spots for your gadgets without needing extension cords. Also, choosing incompatible dimmers or low-quality LED components can cause annoying flickering. Always double-check compatibility! Finally, not considering your electrical panel's capacity can really throw a wrench in things. If your panel can't handle the extra load, you're looking at a bigger project. Getting professional input early can help you avoid these pitfalls and ensure your kitchen's electrical system is safe and functional.
